name: Chiselled look

lead: A chiselled look describes a face whose jaw, cheekbones and chin look sharply defined, as if sculpted. The term is used in looksmaxxing and in everyday talk about male attractiveness.

People pursue it mainly by lowering body and facial fat so that existing bone structure shows, and through grooming and styling. Wikipedia's review of attractiveness research notes that angular male jawlines are preferred in Western countries and that men with low submental fat were rated as having better jawlines.

paras: Common routes include losing body fat, strength training and neck and posture work, grooming such as facial hair and haircuts that frame the jaw, and, for some, dental, filler or surgical changes with clinicians. Some forum users discuss bonesmashing as a route.

Risks depend on the route: aggressive dieting affects health, and practices such as bonesmashing and facial surgery carry documented injury and complication risks. Clinicians are the usual source for procedures.

angle.text: The look is reached mostly by revealing bone structure through leanness and framing it with grooming. Some people add procedures or structural practices on top.

lead: Chiselled look is slang for a face with a sharply defined, angular structure: a clear jawline, prominent cheekbones and a distinct chin. In looksmaxxing it is used as a visual goal and is sometimes tied to practices people believe change facial structure, including bonesmashing.

Research on attractiveness reports that angular male jawlines are preferred in Western countries, that the square chin is mainly a European-heritage trait and so not a universal marker, and that men with low submental fat were rated as having better jawlines [1].
infobox: Angular jaw, defined cheekbones, distinct chin

paras: The term overlaps with 'jawline', 'defined face' and 'sharp features'. It describes a perceived outcome rather than a single technique, so approaches range from diet and grooming to dental and surgical work.

A summary of attractiveness research states that angular jawlines are favoured in Western countries, with men low in submental fat rated as having better jawlines, though the square chin is mainly a European-heritage trait [1]. It also notes that, once perceived health is discounted, one study argued facial masculinity makes little difference to male attractiveness [1].
No studies found on the chiselled look as such. Attractiveness research on jawline preference is summarised above [1].
